title.narrative: Fundacion Avina: Migrants as Agents for Change

description.narrative:
The main objective of the project Migrants as Agents for Change is to strengthen the social fabric of the migrant population through its institutional strengthening and the advocacy capacity of its grassroots organizations in the northern triangle of Central America. The purpose is that, through their strengthening, they themselves can strengthen their bases, participate in spaces of national and regional strategic incidence, as well as make public policy proposals for the defense of their rights, among them, the right to work.
The overall objective is divided into two general objectives: 1) To strengthen the capacity of migrant led organisations to influence policy, legislation and practice at the local and national level and strengthen human rights for migrants. 2) To design multi-sector mechanisms and establish three-party cooperation to support the socio-economic integration of migrants at local level.

Projektet ”Migranter som förändringsagenter-Stärkande av kapacitet för påverkansarbete och ledarskap hos migrantbaserade organisationer i norra triangeln i Centralameriaka (Guatemala, Honduras och El Salvador) genomförs av Fundación Avina under perioden november 2022 – januari 2024. Huvudsyftet med projektet är att stärka organisationsstrukturer hos migranter och återvändare för ökad kapacitet att delta i nationella och regionala processer, utforma och driva förslag till policys som garanterar migranters rättigheter, bland annat rätten att arbeta. Det övergripande målet är uppdelat i två delmål: 1) Att stärka kapaciteten hos migrantledda organisationer att påverka politik, lagstiftning och praxis på lokal och nationell nivå för att stärka migranters mänskliga rättigheter. 2) Att utforma multisektoriella mekanismer och etablera trepartssamarbete, som sammanför lokala myndigheter, den privata sektorn och det civila samhället, för att stödja socioekonomisk integration av migranter på lokal nivå. Fundación Avina är en latinamerikansk organisation med 25 års erfarenhet av att arbeta med migration, stöd till civilsamhället och ekonomiskt stärkande av migranter i Latinamerika. Fundación Avina kommer att samarbeta med 15 lokala organisationer som arbetar med och för migrationer samt med det regionala nätverket av civilsamhällesorganisationer som arbetar med migrationsfrågor.

The project Migrants as agents for change: Strengthening the advocacy and leadership capacity of migrant based organizations in the Northern Triangle in Central America is implemented by Fundación Avina during the period November 2022 – January 2024. The main objective of the project is to strengthen the social fabric of the migrant population through its institutional strengthening and the advocacy capacity of its grassroots organizations in the northern triangle of Central America. The purpose is that, through their strengthening, they themselves can strengthen their bases, participate in spaces of national and regional strategic incidence, as well as make public policy proposals for the defense of their rights, among them, the right to work. The overall objective is divided into two general objectives: 1) To strengthen the capacity of migrant led organizations to influence policy, legislation and practice at the local and national level and strengthen human rights for migrants. 2) To design multi-sector mechanisms and establish three-party cooperation, bringing together local authorities, private sector and civil society, to support the socio-economic integration of migrants at local level. Fundación Avina is a Latin American organization with 25 years of experience of working with migration, support to civil society and economic empowerment of migrants in Latin America. Fundación Avina will collaborate with 15 local organizations working with and for migrations and with the regional network of civil society organizations working on migration issues.

sector.narrative: Facilitation of orderly, safe, regular and responsible migration and mobility

title.narrative: Grant agreement contribution with Fundación Avina 2022

description.narrative:
Objective 1: Strengthened capacities of migrant led organisations to influence policy, legislation and practice at the local and national level and strengthen human rights for migrants.
To achieve this objective Fundación Avina has supported 15 grassroot migrant organizations in Guatemala, El Salvador and Honduras. On the one hand for organizational strengthening, including administrative systems, legal registration, governance, strategic planning and social accountability and on the other hand to strengthen networking, alliance-building, advocacy, strategic communication and knowledge building. Special attention has been given to womens leadership and empowerment e.g. through a womens leadership program trained 45 migrant women leaders.
Examples of organizational advances made by Honduran organizations include the grass root organization CONAMIREDIS that obtained legal status after more than 15 years of organizing, increasing its autonomy, fundraising capacity, and participation in national and regional advocacy spaces. Likewise in Honduras ARJUC strengthened its organizational systems and participated in a four-month human rights training program enhancing the advocacy capacities. In El Salvador ASCAPER was established as a savings and credit cooperative for returned migrants, expanding financial services for migrants and their families. In Guatemala DESGUA developed a strategic plan and secured official certification for its culinary training school, improving participants employment opportunities.
A key element of the support to the organizations has been the strengthening of communication and advocacy capabilities and increased participation in regional and national networks. At least 10 organizations actively presented policy proposals and recommendations and implemented initiatives aimed at influencing migration-related policies and programs.
Examples of advocacy and its results include: GUND in Guatemala engaged with congress and government institutions to develop and promote reforms to regulations governing overseas labor recruitment agencies. CONAMIREDIS in Honduras contributed to the validation of the National Reintegration Plan 20242025. COFAMIDE in El Salvador worked to update proposed legislation on the search for missing migrants and COFAMIPRO in Honduras developed advocacy strategies and social accountability tools related to the search for missing migrants.
During 2025 the organizations deepened their participation in regional and international forums, including the Regional Conference on Migration, the Central American Parliament and processes linked to the Global Compact for Migration. Organizations prepared policy inputs, participated in consultations, and engaged directly with decision-makers. A notable example was a forum in Guatemala Roots that Travel, which brought together migrant organizations, government institutions, international organizations, and migrant workers to discuss ethical labor mobility. The forum generated recommendations that were shared with public authorities.
The overall result related to this objective is that the project significantly strengthened migrant grassroots organizations institutional capacity, leadership, networking, and advocacy skills. As a result, these organizations increased their influence in public policy discussions and decision-making processes related to labor mobility, migrant rights, reintegration, and the search for missing migrants at local, national, regional, and international levels.
In addition, the project supported the the Regional Network of Civil Society Organizations for Migration (RROCM) and the development of its Regional Strategic Agenda 20252026, thereby aligning the priorities and proposals of migrant-led organizations with a shared regional roadmap. At least seven migrant-led organizations from Guatemala, Honduras, and El Salvador actively contributed to this process and strengthened their strategic advocacy capacity within the RROCM. 14 organizations established new alliances through networks and working groups, while 12 joined collaborative advocacy agendas. Womens leadership and participation within regional coordination spaces were actively encouraged and support to womens participation in in regional events helped strengthen leadership and collaboration.
Communication was a cross-cutting component throughout the project. Efforts focused on increasing the visibility of migrant-led organizations through development of narratives, media engagement, spokesperson training, and communication toolkits. In 2023, a regional communication workshop brought together more than 60 participants from Central America, leading to the production of 19 audiovisual pieces related to migration and labor issues. Through partnerships with other organizations, training activities, media engagement, and content production ethical and rights-based migration reporting and new migration narratives were promoted.
Overall, the project significantly enhanced the advocacy capacity of migrant-led organizations by increasing their participation in dialogue and decision-making spaces, strengthening collective agendas, generating evidence for policy discussions, and using strategic communication to position their priorities in the public sphere.
Objective 2: Mechanisms designed and established for three-party cooperation to support the socioeconomic integration of migrants at local level
Fundación Avina promoted a three-party model of local socioeconomic inclusion of migrants that involves various government agencies, the private sector and civil society. The organizational strengthening and capacity building promoted by the project allowed some of the grassroots organizations to become actively involved in local initiatives aimed at promoting alliances with the local governments, companies and other actors, in order to promote socioeconomic inclusion initiatives.
As a result, five multisectoral coordination mechanisms were established in different cities. These brought together public institutions, civil society organizations, private companies, and international cooperation actors to provide coordinated services to support inclusion of migrants and returnees, such as psychosocial assistance, documentation, training, skills certification, financial inclusion, entrepreneurship support, and employment guidance.
In several local initiatives the tripartite cooperation was key for progress, examples include the My First Job program led by Fundación HAME in Guatemala, which certified 58 migrants for labor market insertion and a coordination mechanism promoted in Honduras by the Choloma Chamber of Commerce and Industry linked to the municipal mobility policy. As a direct result, 305 people in human mobility participated in socioeconomic inclusion initiatives, including training, certification, employment placement, entrepreneurship development, and access to credit.
Significant progress was also achieved in local public policy development. In Choloma (Honduras) the first Municipal Public Policy on Human Mobility was adopted in September 2024, while in Guatemala municipal migration policies were advanced in Olintepeque and Coatepeque. In El Salvador, a Territorial Strategic Plan for the Socioeconomic Inclusion of Migrants was developed in the Cayaguanca region.
The project also supported participation in relevant regional forums, including the OECD Local Development Forum 2025, where experiences on socioeconomic inclusion models were shared and opportunities for regional collaboration were explored.
Throughout the project implementation migrant-led organizations participated actively in shaping actions, contributing to public policy development, and engaging with the private sector on employment, and entrepreneurship. Although results varied across municipalities depending on local conditions and stakeholder engagement, the overall outcome reflects significant progress in building multisectoral coordination, advancing local public policies, and creating economic opportunities for migrants and returnees.
